name: The Comparison Lab
summary: A product-review identity that puts alternatives on one evidence desk with equal schematics, stable labels and visible revision status.

palette.name: Text
palette.evidence: Dominant text-run color in source richSlides

palette.name: Accent
palette.evidence: Observed direct source color; this reusable accent role is an editorial choice, not an inferred original token.

typography.usage: Large comparison titles and short conclusions.
Concept IDs, revision and specification labels.

recognitionRules: Keep a numbered vertical rail and revision line on every page.
Use monospaced labels for concepts and measured specifications.
Give each concept an equal-sized schematic panel.
Use teal and rust for distinct comparison functions, not winner and loser decoration.

principles: Move from observation to interpretation to a bounded next question.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: Three concepts. The same questions. A decision worth testing.
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid “proves” when the material only supports a hypothesis.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: A record suggests a direction; it does not speak for every person.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use THE COMPARISON LAB in Arial with a compact Courier revision code and three equal vertical strokes. No flask icon.
invariants: Keep a numbered vertical rail and revision line on every page.
Use monospaced labels for concepts and measured specifications.
Give each concept an equal-sized schematic panel.
adaptations: A short review can use one shared comparison spread.
Retain concept IDs when moving from schematic to physical prototype.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.
